// This is the stand-in SYSTEM UNDER TEST for the harness's own integration
// tier. It is materialized and compiled at test time rather than shipped as a
// package, because the module deliberately has no main.
//
// It does the two things a harnessed service must do, and nothing else: read its
// configuration off disk from the path it is given, and read its secret from the
// environment. The in-process entrypoint in the same test implements the same
// contract, so RunParity proves a real subprocess and a real in-process run agree.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: artifact <config-path>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	content, err := os.ReadFile(os.Args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "config unreadable: "+err.Error())
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	service := ""
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(content), "\n") {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "service:") {
			service = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "service:"))
		}
	}
	fmt.Println("service=" + service)
	fmt.Println("secret=" + os.Getenv("ATOMI_POSTGRES__MAIN__PASSWORD"))
	if raw := os.Getenv("E2E_ARTIFACT_EXIT"); raw != "" {
		code, convErr := strconv.Atoi(raw)
		if convErr != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "bad exit code: "+raw)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if code != 0 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "requested failure")
			os.Exit(code)
		}
	}
}
